tagline.text: The Philippines' top hands-on science museum, in the heart of BGC

location.label: Location
location.text: J. Y. Campos Park, 3rd Avenue, Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (indoors), crowded on weekends and school holidays

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600–1,500 (per person, covering tickets, meals and transport)

children.text: The Mind Museum is a hands-on science museum that opened in Bonifacio Global City in 2012, with more than 250 exhibits spread across five galleries. It is air-conditioned, which makes it a good way to spend half a day in Manila with children.

The Mind Museum is a science museum in Bonifacio Global City (BGC) in Taguig, part of Metro Manila. It sits in J. Y. Campos Park on a lot of about 1.2 hectares and officially opened on March 16, 2012. It is run by the Bonifacio Art Foundation (BAFI), and its building was designed by architect Ed Calma (Lor Calma & Partners), reportedly inspired by the structure and growth of cells. That the Philippines gained a full-scale science museum like this was news in itself, and it matters that about 90 percent of the exhibits are said to have been made by Filipino designers, scientists and fabricators. Wikipedia records that in 2014 it won the THEA Award in the science museum category, the first time an Asian science museum received it.

The exhibits are divided into five themes: atom, life, earth, universe and technology. The atom, life, earth and universe galleries are on the ground floor, and the largest gallery, technology, is on the upper floor. The galleries are linked by passages called Nature's Webways. There are more than 250 exhibits in all, covering an exhibit area of about 4,900 square meters. The best-known sight is Stan in the earth gallery, a Tyrannosaurus rex fossil about
(40 feet) long that is presented as the first permanently displayed T. rex in the Philippines. A life-size whale shark (butanding) is also impressive.

Rather than just looking, you can press and turn many of the exhibits with your own hands, which makes the museum especially popular with children. Programs include science demonstrations held at set times (Mind Moving Studios), a planetarium called Space Shell where you watch space films, and the Nature Hour Glass, which screens nature films. The museum also stages traveling exhibitions that tour the Philippines each year, such as Space Adventure, which imitates a Mars base, and Dino Play, a fossil-digging game. Traveling and special exhibitions may not be included in the admission ticket, so check before you book.

BGC is a planned district with shopping malls, cafes and parks, so it is easy to add a meal and a walk before and after the museum. It suits families with children in Manila, science lovers and anyone looking for an indoor plan on a bad-weather day. Entry works on time slots, and popular slots fill up early, so booking online is recommended. Ticket prices and hours change often, so check the official site for the latest information. Prices in this guide come from 2026 travel blogs, though some, such as student rates, include 2019 information. For its 14th anniversary in March 2026, the museum sold 3-hour tickets for ₱14 and gave free passes to children born in 2012. Promotions like this change every year, so keep an eye on its social media announcements. BGC's wide sidewalks and parks make it pleasant to stroll past malls, cafes and street sculptures after the museum. Restaurants get busy in the evening, so families should consider reserving.
The signature exhibit of the earth gallery is Stan, a Tyrannosaurus rex fossil about
long. It is known as the first permanently displayed T. rex in the Philippines and makes a great photo spot.
This gallery lets you touch and understand invisible forces such as gravity and electromagnetism. With many hands-on devices, it is especially popular with elementary school children.

This gallery covers the diversity of life, from the smallest organisms to large habitats. It shows how the sizes of living things and their habitats connect in one flow, which suits children interested in living things.
This gallery shows how the universe began and how stars and planets move. It is easier to understand when combined with the Space Shell planetarium.
The largest gallery, it looks at how technology changes everyday life. It also covers themes such as creativity, innovation and values, so even middle schoolers and older visitors will not get bored.

Mind Moving Studios holds science demonstrations at set times, and on Saturday mornings there are sometimes liquid nitrogen demonstrations. Program schedules change, so check the notice when you enter. On most Sundays at 5 PM, programs such as Awesome Astronomy, a talk about the stars and astronomy, and Cafe Scientifique, a discussion of science topics, have been announced.

Past exhibitions have included Space Adventure, a Mars base experience, Dino Play, a fossil dig, and The Teenage Brain, on brain science. Exhibitions change with the season and may carry a separate fee. There have also been rotating exhibitions such as A Glass of the Sea, about the sea, and Forever Lab, about time and symbols.

blocks.title: Space Shell and Nature Hour Glass

children.text: The Space Shell planetarium, where you watch space films, and the Nature Hour Glass, which screens nature films, are set up as separate spaces. Check the on-site notices for showtimes and whether an extra fee applies. After one visit, what you saw in the galleries becomes easier to grasp in three dimensions.

items.title: Half-day science museum route
items.subtitle: Making the most of a 3-hour ticket

children.text: Arrive for the first time slot, confirm your ticket and enter. Popular slots get crowded, so have your reserved ticket ready.
Go through the atom, life, earth and universe galleries on the ground floor in order, starting with places where your child can touch things.
Take photos in front of Stan the dinosaur and finish the earth gallery.
See the technology gallery on the upper floor. If the timing works, stop by Mind Moving Studios for a demonstration.
When your entry time ends, have lunch at a BGC mall or restaurant.

A 3-hour ticket means you must leave when time is up, so visit the galleries you most want to see first. An all-day pass lets you stay without a time limit. If your child is young, it is fine to stay long in one gallery. Rather than trying to see everything, it is more fun to spend your time where your child lingers longest. Check the locations of stairs and elevators on the guide map when you enter.

items.title: Full-day family route in BGC
items.subtitle: The science museum and a city walk

children.text: Start at a relaxed pace with an all-day pass at the museum.
Have lunch at the BGC dining area near the museum.
In the afternoon, return to the museum to see exhibits and demonstrations you missed.
Stroll through BGC's parks and streets and rest at a cafe.
Have dinner and return to your hotel by Grab.
It takes about
40 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
by taxi or Grab from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to BGC, depending heavily on the time of day.
If you are staying in Makati, it takes about
15–40 minutes
by taxi to BGC.
Rush hours are very congested, so allow extra time in your plans.
Take the MRT to Ayala Station, then catch the BGC West route bus at McKinley Exchange toward Market! Market!.
Then transfer to the BGC Central bus, get off near Net One and walk the rest of the way. Routes and fares may change, so check locally.
You can reach it via C5, Kalayaan Avenue, Lawton Avenue, McKinley Road and others, and the museum is on 3rd Avenue in J. Y. Campos Park.
The museum has no parking lot of its own. A flat rate of about ₱50 is said to apply at the Crescent North parking with receipt validation, so confirm locally.
If you take Grab or a taxi, get off near the museum's front entrance on 3rd Avenue and walk in. Roads may be closed during events, so it is fine to get off a block or two before.
It is an indoor attraction, so you can go year-round. It makes a good indoor plan in the rainy season and a cool escape in the hot summer months.
It gets crowded on weekends, school holidays and field trip season. For a quieter visit, choose a weekday morning and ask the museum about group tour schedules.

BGC has many hotels and serviced apartments, and Makati and Ortigas are also a short taxi ride away. If you stay in BGC with children, you can walk between the museum, the malls and the parks. Prices and reviews change a lot by season, so check them on a booking site. If you book in BGC for a day at the museum, checking the schedule of weekend events and races helps you avoid higher room rates and traffic jams.

BGC offers plenty of choices, from Filipino food to Japanese, Korean, cafes and food halls. Around the nearby Market! Market! mall and the high street you can pick almost any restaurant, which makes meals easy for families. Check locally for the rules on bringing outside food.
If you reserve a time slot online, you can enter without waiting in line.
Student and teacher discounts require an official ID, so be sure to bring it.
To avoid days with many school groups, email the museum to ask.
For the birthday discount, an announcement said a government-issued ID or a birth certificate with a photo was required for walk-in purchase, so check ahead.
It is cool indoors, so dress children in a light jacket.
Traveling and special exhibitions may not be included in the admission ticket.
For demonstrations such as Mind Moving Studios, check the schedule when you enter.
BGC is good for walking, but midday is hot and the sun is strong, so bring a hat and water.
After your visit, check the next demonstration and showtimes again at the information desk near the entrance. That makes it easier to plan a return trip the same day to see what you missed.
Ticket prices and hours change often. The prices in this guide come from August 2026 travel blogs and partly from 2019, so be sure to check the official site.
The museum is closed on Mondays, so visit between Tuesday and Sunday.
Entry is by time slot, so with a 3-hour ticket you must leave when your time is up.
Parking fees in BGC and roads around the museum get congested during events, so consider public transport and Grab together.
Keep valuables on you at all times and do not let go of your child's hand. On crowded days, agree on a meeting place with your child before you go in.
The planned district where the museum stands, with malls, cafes and parks, good for a meal and a walk after your visit.
A financial and commercial center a short taxi ride from BGC, with the Ayala malls and many restaurants.
A shopping and dining complex reached by taxi, a good choice for dinner.
